topics.title: Meaning, Objective & Scope of AS 19
explain: A lease is an agreement where the lessor conveys the right to use an asset to the lessee for an agreed time in return for periodic payments.
AS 19 prescribes accounting policies and disclosures for both lessees and lessors for finance and operating leases.
Lease agreements for natural resources exploration like oil, gas, timber, and minerals are excluded from AS 19.
Licensing agreements for motion picture films, video recordings, plays, patents, and copyrights are excluded.
Lease agreements to use land are also specifically excluded from the scope of AS 19.

flow.title: AS 19 Scope Applicability Test
steps: Check if agreement conveys asset usage right
Verify if asset is land
Verify if it involves natural resource exploration
Verify if it is an IP licensing agreement
If all exclusions fail AS 19 applies

topics.example: A company leasing a factory machine for 5 years is covered under AS 19, whereas leasing land or oil exploration rights is excluded.
remember: Land leases, natural resources exploration, and IP licensing agreements are excluded from AS 19.
mistakes: Applying AS 19 rules to land lease agreements, which are specifically out of scope.

quiz.q: Which of the following transactions falls under the scope of AS 19?
quiz.why: Land, natural resource exploration, and IP licensing are explicitly excluded from AS 19.

quiz.q: Who is the party that conveys the right to use an asset in a lease agreement?
quiz.why: The lessor is the legal owner who conveys the right to use the asset to the lessee.

topics.title: Key Definitions in Lease Accounting
explain: Inception of lease is the earlier of the lease agreement date or commitment date by parties to principal provisions.
Lease term is the non-cancellable period plus option periods reasonably certain to be exercised by the lessee.
Minimum Lease Payments (MLP) for lessee include rentals plus residual value guaranteed by or on behalf of lessee.
Gross Investment (GI) equals MLP plus Unguaranteed Residual Value (UGRV) accruing to the lessor.
Net Investment (NI) is the present value of Gross Investment discounted at the interest rate implicit in the lease.
Unearned Finance Income (UFI) is the difference between Gross Investment and Net Investment.
Interest rate implicit in lease is the discount rate that makes present value of (MLP + UGRV) equal to asset fair value.

flow.title: Gross to Net Investment & UFI Flow
steps: Aggregate lease rents and Guaranteed Residual Value
Add Unguaranteed Residual Value to get Gross Investment
Discount cash inflows at implicit rate for Net Investment
Deduct Net Investment from Gross Investment for UFI

topics.example: If total cash inflows over lease term plus UGRV equal ₹43 lakhs (GI) and their present value is ₹28.3 lakhs (NI), Unearned Finance Income is ₹14.7 lakhs.
remember: Unearned Finance Income (UFI) = Gross Investment - Net Investment
mistakes: Including contingent rent or service costs inside Minimum Lease Payments (MLP).

quiz.q: How is Unearned Finance Income (UFI) calculated under AS 19?
o: Total Rent minus Guaranteed Residual Value
quiz.why: UFI is defined as the difference between Gross Investment and Net Investment in the lease.

quiz.q: Which of the following is EXCLUDED while calculating Minimum Lease Payments (MLP)?
quiz.why: Contingent rent, costs for services, and taxes reimbursed to lessor are excluded from MLP.

topics.title: Classification of Leases (Finance vs Operating)
explain: Lease classification depends on substance over form: whether substantially all risks and rewards of ownership transfer.
Finance Lease transfers substantially all risks and rewards incidental to ownership (title may or may not transfer).
Operating Lease does not transfer substantially all risks and rewards incidental to ownership.
AS 19 gives 5 deterministic conditions; if ANY 1 condition is met, the lease is classified as a finance lease.
Deterministic conditions: ownership transfer, bargain purchase option, major economic life covered, PV of MLP >= fair value, or specialized asset.
3 suggestive conditions also exist (lessee bears cancellation loss, residual value changes accrue to lessee, low secondary period rent).
Classification is determined at the inception of the lease and is not revised for changes in estimates.

flow.title: Lease Classification Decision Flow
steps: Check for ownership transfer at term end
Check for bargain purchase option
Check if lease covers major economic life
Check if PV of MLP covers fair value
Check if asset is highly specialized
If any 1 test passes classify as Finance Lease

topics.example: A hospital leases specially designed ambulances usable only by that hospital. Because the asset is specialized, it is a Finance Lease.
remember: Meeting ANY ONE of the 5 deterministic conditions makes a lease a Finance Lease.
Classification is made at inception and not changed for simple estimate revisions.
mistakes: Thinking all 5 deterministic conditions must be satisfied to classify a lease as a Finance Lease.

quiz.q: How many deterministic conditions must be met to classify a lease as a Finance Lease under AS 19?
quiz.why: Meeting any single deterministic condition normally leads to finance lease classification.

quiz.q: What is the primary basis for classifying a lease under AS 19?
quiz.why: Classification depends on whether risks and rewards incidental to ownership are transferred.

topics.title: Accounting for Finance Leases in Books of Lessee
explain: At inception, lessee recognizes the asset and corresponding liability at LOWER of Fair Value or Present Value of MLP.
Discount rate for PV is interest rate implicit in lease; if not determinable, use lessee's incremental borrowing rate.
Journal entry at inception: Asset A/c Dr. to Lessor A/c (at lower of Fair Value and PV of MLP).
Lease payments are split into Finance Charge (interest expense) and reduction of outstanding lease liability.
Finance charge is allocated to produce a constant periodic rate of interest on the remaining balance of liability.
Asset is depreciated as per AS 10. If ownership transfer is uncertain, depreciate over shorter of useful life or lease term.

flow.title: Lessee Accounting Process for Finance Lease
steps: Compare Fair Value and PV of MLP
Record asset and liability at lower amount
Make periodic lease rental payment
Apportion payment into interest and principal reduction
Charge finance cost to P&L Account
Calculate depreciation over shorter of life or term

topics.example: Fair value of leased equipment is ₹20 lakhs and PV of MLP is ₹18.55 lakhs. Lessee recognizes asset and liability at ₹18.55 lakhs.
remember: Lessee records asset/liability at LOWER of Fair Value and PV of MLP.
Depreciate over shorter of useful life or lease term if ownership transfer is uncertain.
mistakes: Deducting the lease liability from the asset in the balance sheet instead of presenting it as a separate liability.

quiz.q: At what value does the lessee recognize a finance lease at inception?
o: Lower of Fair Value and Present Value of MLP
Higher of Fair Value and Present Value of MLP
quiz.why: AS 19 requires initial recognition at the lower of fair value and present value of minimum lease payments.

quiz.q: If ownership transfer at lease end is uncertain, over what period should the lessee depreciate the asset?
o: Shorter of useful life or lease term
Longer of useful life or lease term
quiz.why: Without reasonable certainty of ownership, asset is depreciated over shorter of lease term or useful life.

topics.title: Accounting for Finance Leases in Books of Lessor
explain: Lessor recognizes leased asset as receivable at an amount equal to Net Investment in the lease (usually Fair Value).
Entry at inception: Lease Receivable A/c Dr. to Asset A/c at Net Investment.
Unearned Finance Income (UFI) = Gross Investment minus Net Investment.
UFI is recognized as finance income in P&L over the lease term on a pattern reflecting constant periodic rate of return.
Initial direct costs are either expensed immediately or allocated against finance income over the lease term.
Lessor regularly reviews Unguaranteed Residual Value (UGRV). Downward revisions adjust income allocation immediately; upward adjustments are ignored.
Manufacturer or dealer lessor recognizes selling profit/loss at inception (Fair Value minus Cost) and expenses initial direct costs.

flow.title: Lessor Finance Lease Workflow
steps: Calculate Gross Investment and Net Investment
Record Lease Receivable at Net Investment
Receive periodic lease rentals
Split rental into principal reduction and finance income
Recognize finance income in P&L Account
Review UGRV and adjust for reductions only

topics.example: Lessor leases machine costing ₹28.3 lakhs with Gross Investment ₹43 lakhs. Net Investment is ₹28.3 lakhs and UFI of ₹14.69 lakhs is recognized over 5 years.
remember: Lessor records Lease Receivable at Net Investment.
Upward adjustments to estimated unguaranteed residual value are NEVER made.
mistakes: Making upward adjustments to estimated residual value when market prices increase.

quiz.q: In a finance lease, at what amount does the lessor record the lease receivable at inception?
quiz.why: Lessor records asset given on finance lease as receivable equal to Net Investment in the lease.

quiz.q: What action does a lessor take if estimated unguaranteed residual value increases?
quiz.why: AS 19 explicitly prohibits upward adjustment of estimated unguaranteed residual value.

topics.title: Accounting for Operating Leases
explain: In an operating lease, risks and rewards remain with lessor; the asset stays in the lessor's Balance Sheet under PPE.
Lessee recognizes lease payments as expense in P&L on a Straight-Line Basis (SLM) over lease term, unless another systematic basis fits benefit pattern.
Difference between lease rent due and rent expense recognized on SLM is transferred to Lease Equalisation Account.
Lessor recognizes lease rent as income on a Straight-Line Basis in P&L over lease term.
Lessor charges depreciation under AS 10 and tests asset for impairment under AS 28.
Manufacturer/dealer lessor does NOT recognize selling profit on operating lease because it is not equivalent to sales.

flow.title: Operating Lease Rental Expense Flow
steps: Sum total rent payable over lease term
Calculate annual SLM expense
Compare annual SLM expense with rent due
Transfer difference to Lease Equalisation Account
Charge annual SLM expense to P&L

topics.example: Total rent over 3 years is ₹1,20,000 for output pattern 10k, 20k, 50k units. P&L rent expense based on output is ₹15,000, ₹30,000, and ₹75,000 respectively.
remember: Operating lease expense/income is recognized on Straight-Line Basis (SLM) unless another systematic basis fits better.
Depreciation is claimed ONLY by the lessor in an operating lease.
mistakes: Charging depreciation in lessee's books for an operating lease.

quiz.q: How should a lessee recognize operating lease payments in the statement of Profit & Loss?
o: On straight-line basis over lease term
quiz.why: Operating lease payments are recognized on a straight-line basis over the lease term unless another systematic basis is more representative.

quiz.q: Who claims depreciation on the leased asset in an operating lease?
quiz.why: In operating lease, the asset remains on lessor's balance sheet, so lessor claims depreciation.

topics.title: Sale and Leaseback Transactions
explain: In sale and leaseback, an owner sells an asset for cash and immediately leases it back from the buyer.
If leaseback is a Finance Lease: Any profit or loss (sale proceeds minus carrying amount) is deferred and amortized over lease term in proportion to depreciation.
If leaseback is an Operating Lease and Sale Price = Fair Value: Profit or loss is recognized IMMEDIATELY in P&L.
If Sale Price < Fair Value: Profit/loss recognized immediately, UNLESS loss is compensated by future below-market rents (then defer and amortize loss over usage period).
If Sale Price > Fair Value: Excess profit over Fair Value MUST be deferred and amortized over expected usage period.
In operating leaseback, if Fair Value < Carrying Amount at transaction date: Immediate loss equal to (Carrying Amount - Fair Value) is recognized.

flow.title: Operating Sale and Leaseback Evaluation Flow
steps: Compare Carrying Amount with Fair Value
If Fair Value is lower write down asset immediately
Compare Sale Price with Fair Value
If Sale Price equals Fair Value recognize profit immediately
If Sale Price exceeds Fair Value defer excess profit
If Sale Price is below Fair Value check for rent compensation

topics.example: Asset with WDV ₹40 lakhs sold for ₹50 lakhs when Fair Value is ₹40 lakhs (operating leaseback). Profit of ₹10 lakhs (excess over FV) is deferred and amortized over lease period.
remember: Finance leaseback profit/loss is ALWAYS deferred and amortized.
Operating leaseback excess sale price over fair value MUST be deferred and amortized.
mistakes: Recognizing full profit immediately when sale price exceeds fair value in an operating leaseback.

quiz.q: In a sale and leaseback resulting in a Finance Lease, how is the profit on sale treated by seller-lessee?
o: Deferred and amortized over lease term in proportion to depreciation
quiz.why: Any profit/loss in a finance leaseback is deferred and amortized over the lease term in proportion to depreciation.

quiz.q: In an operating leaseback, if Sale Price (₹50L) exceeds Fair Value (₹40L) while WDV is ₹40L, how is the ₹10L profit treated?
o: Deferred and amortized over expected usage period
quiz.why: The excess of sale price over fair value in an operating leaseback must be deferred and amortized.
